Where the results differ from vegan

Source: vignettes/differences-from-vegan.Rmd
differences-from-vegan.Rmd

Every function in ecolongr is compared with the vegan call it replaces in the tests. Distances, standardisations, diversity indices and expected richness equal vegan’s to about 1e-10, and PCA scores to about 1e-8 (1e-6 with the iterative solver on large tables), apart from the cases below. The tests use varespec, BCI and a synthetic community, including all-zero samples and explicit zero rows.

Alpha diversity

  • el_rrarefy() is random and does not give vegan’s subsample for the same seed. vegan::rrarefy() draws the individuals one at a time. el_rrarefy() draws the count of each taxon from the hypergeometric distribution of what is left, which costs one draw per taxon. Both draw from the same distribution of counts, and the tests compare the mean and the variance of every cell over many replicates with vegan’s and with the exact values. The table is read into R, so this function needs a few times the memory of its input.
  • el_rrarefy(), el_drarefy() and el_rarefy() drop samples with a total below depth, with a warning that names them. vegan::rrarefy() returns such a sample unchanged, which leaves samples of different depths in the result. vegan::drarefy() and vegan::rarefy() treat depth as the sample total, so the values are not for a common depth. If no sample reaches depth it is an error. Without a depth, all three use the smallest sample total, which vegan has no default for. With check = FALSE, el_drarefy() and el_rarefy() drop silently.
  • el_rarefy() has no se, and takes one depth. The standard error needs a sum over pairs of taxa. Call the function once for each depth.
  • A sample with no non-zero row is absent from the result of el_specnumber(), el_diversity() and el_rarefy(). vegan gives an all-zero row Shannon 0, Simpson 1, inverse Simpson Inf and richness 0.
  • groups, MARGIN and the other alpha-diversity functions (renyi(), fisher.alpha(), estimateR(), specpool()) are not implemented.
  • The input has one row per sample and taxon. A duplicated pair counts as two taxa, where vegan has already summed them in the matrix.

Beta diversity

  • el_decostand("rclr") leaves zeros absent. vegan’s decostand(x, "rclr") fills the zeros with values from a matrix completion, so every cell becomes non-zero. Like clr, that cannot be returned as a table without zeros. The completion is also one global fit over all observed cells, which a lazy table query cannot express. el_decostand("rclr") therefore does only the part that fits: the log-ratio of the non-zero cells. The completion also changes the non-zero cells; el_decostand("rclr") matches decostand(x, "rclr", impute = FALSE). A later step that reads absent cells as 0 puts those taxa at the sample’s geometric mean, so Euclidean distance on it is not vegan’s robust.aitchison when the table has zeros. For that, use el_vegdist(method = "robust.aitchison") or el_rda(transform = "rclr") on the raw counts: they run the same matrix completion as vegan, of rank 3 unless you set ropt, on the observed cells only and agree with vegan to about 1e-6. They need every sample to have at least one non-zero cell.
  • clr needs a prevalence filter in practice. On a 414-sample, 60,633-ASV time series with 99% zeros, PC1–PC2 of a clr PCA showed the seasonal cycle poorly (seasonal R² 0.28), but as well as Hellinger once ASVs present in fewer than 20% of the samples were removed (0.64). Filter with duckplyr verbs before the call: semi_join() against the ASVs with n_distinct(sample) >= 0.2 * n_distinct(all samples).
  • metaMDS() on the dist has no species scores. Given a community matrix, metaMDS() also computes species scores as weighted averages and applies its own automatic transformations (autotransform). That needs the dense matrix, which is what this package avoids. On a dist you get the sample scores only: ordination$species is NA and scores(ordination, display = "species") is empty. Transform with el_decostand() before el_vegdist() instead.
  • log follows vegan without the warning: if any value is not a whole number, everything is first divided by the smallest positive value in the table.
  • hellinger writes a temporary Parquet file, because duckplyr cannot compute a square root. The file is removed when the R session ends.
  • Bray–Curtis and Jaccard need non-negative quantities. Euclidean distance and el_rda() accept negative ones, for example after rclr.

Ordination

  • el_rda() returns the first k axes only. scores(), eigenvals(), plot() and screeplot() work. predict() and fitted() need the full matrix and give an error. anova() gives vegan’s table for an unconstrained ordination, which has no constrained component. Axis signs are arbitrary, as in vegan.
  • k sets the number of axes (default 5). A k above the rank, min(number of samples − 1, number of taxa), is silently reduced to it, so a very large k returns all axes, as a full PCA. A k close to the rank makes el_rda() use the exact solver, which builds the dense samples × taxa matrix. Keep k small on large tables, where the iterative solver is used. With transform = "rclr" there are at most ropt axes, the rank of the completion (default 3, as vegan’s ropt).
  • The variance the k axes leave out is known, and el_rda() reports it in a message. pca$tot.chi is the total variance of the whole table, whatever k is, so 1 - sum(vegan::eigenvals(pca)) / pca$tot.chi is the unexplained share. Only that sum is known: the eigenvalues of the axes beyond k are not. Silence the message with suppressMessages() or options(ecolongr.quiet = TRUE).
  • Divide an eigenvalue by tot.chi, never by the sum of the eigenvalues. vegan::eigenvals(pca) / sum(vegan::eigenvals(pca)) sums to one over the k axes whatever k is, and so hides the variance that the other axes hold. vegan::eigenvals(pca) / pca$tot.chi and summary(pca) give the share of the whole.
  • Some plotting packages divide by the sum of the eigenvalues and so mislabel the axes. ggordiplots (ord_labels(), used by its ordination plot functions) and microViz (ord_plot()) put a percentage in the axis label that is the eigenvalue divided by the sum of the kept eigenvalues, so the k labels sum to 100%. Labels from eigenvals(pca) / pca$tot.chi, as above, are right; replace the axis titles of such a plot with them, for example with ggplot2::xlab(). ggvegan::autoplot() does not print percentages and works on the result. For transform = "rclr" the share is 0, because the completed matrix has rank ropt, and the axes hold all of it.
